hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Pipeline-integrated external-service graph tracing. The graph gains one new node kind (ExternalEndpoint, carrying a protocol + resolved/unresolved tag) and four typed boundary edge kinds (CALLS_HTTP, PUBLISHES_TO, SUBSCRIBES_TO, CALLS_RPC), added once to the graph vocabulary and gated by a graph-schema migration so existing indexes evolve without a full re-index. Per-language outbound and inbound detectors run as thin plugins inside the existing tree-sitter parse; a shared protocol-agnostic resolution engine turns indirect/configured targets into a concrete identity (or an explicit unresolved marker) from layered config sources with a fixed precedence. Cross-repo linking is a separate daemon-side matching pass, keyed off a per-repo service-identity registry, that forms a real dependency edge onto the target repo's actual handler entity and inserts it into the DEPENDS_ON closure; the same pass, re-fired on repo register/re-index events, is the out-of-order backfill.

consumedContracts.name: ExternalEndpoint graph vocabulary
consumedContracts.purpose: The first-class node kind + four typed boundary edge kinds for external-service dependencies, the per-repo deterministic endpoint id, and their participation in the DEPENDS_ON closure. Foundation every detector + the matcher writes into.

consumedContracts.name: Target resolution engine
consumedContracts.purpose: Turn an indirect/configured outbound target expression into a concrete identity, or an explicit unresolved marker, using layered config sources with a fixed precedence. A pure resolver consumed by every outbound detector.

boundary.internal: The per-language (TS/Python/Go/Java/Scala) HTTP-client call-site recognition patterns — which client libraries and call shapes count as an outbound HTTP call, and how the URL argument expression is extracted for handing to the resolver — are entirely internal to S003; nothing else consumes S003's detector.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — Detection: outbound classes + inbound handlers + service identity

nonFunctional.performance: Detection reuses the single existing tree-sitter parse per file — no second parse pass is added to indexing. The cross-repo matching pass is bounded per registry/re-index event (it re-evaluates only endpoints whose match could have changed), not a full-workspace rescan on every index.
nonFunctional.security: Detection is static and at-rest — config, .env, k8s, and docker sources are read as text, never executed (k6). Resolution uses config/secret values only to derive a service IDENTITY (host/topic/service string) recorded as the endpoint target; raw secret contents beyond the resolved identity string are not persisted as graph data.
nonFunctional.observability: Unresolved endpoints are first-class and queryable (they carry the raw expression), so coverage gaps are visible rather than silent; cross-repo edges vs endpoint-only outcomes are distinguishable so an operator can see where matching did and did not link.
nonFunctional.durability: New nodes/edges use deterministic ids (repo + resolved target), and the vocabulary lands behind a graph-schema migration, so re-indexing is stable and idempotent and existing indexes evolve without a destructive full rebuild.

api.name: parse
api.signature: parse(filePath: string, source: string, repo: string): ParseResult

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: Repo root, already threaded into makeEntityId (unchanged).

returns.meaning: { entities, relations } — SIGNATURE UNCHANGED. S003 extends the existing call_expression visitors in each of the 5 parsers with a thin HTTP-client recognizer: when a call-site matches a known HTTP client shape, it pushes an UNRESOLVED CALLS_HTTP relation `{ kind:'CALLS_HTTP', from:<calling code entity id>, to:<raw URL argument expression>, resolved:false }` into relations. No new ParseResult field; no second parse pass (performance NF). Non-HTTP call-sites are unaffected (still emit CALLS).

preconditions: The parser already visits call_expression nodes for CALLS emission (the recognizer hooks the same visit).
postconditions: An HTTP call-site yields exactly one unresolved CALLS_HTTP relation whose `to` is the raw URL expression; a repo with no HTTP calls yields a byte-identical ParseResult to before.

api.name: resolve
api.signature: resolve(repo: string, protocol: ExternalProtocol, rawExpression: string): Promise<ResolvedTarget>

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: Repo whose at-rest config sources scope resolution (sc2).

parameters.name: protocol
parameters.purpose: Always 'http' for this detector — carried onto the resolved endpoint.

parameters.name: rawExpression
parameters.purpose: The raw URL argument expression captured at the call-site.

returns.meaning: sc2 (S002) — CONSUMED unchanged. {resolved:true, protocol:'http', identity} for a pinnable URL, else {resolved:false, rawExpression}. Called once per repo in the async post-parse pass (sc2 memoizes the ConfigSourceMap per repo).

preconditions: Runs in the async post-parse pass (not in the sync parse), so awaiting resolve is legal.
postconditions: Deterministic: same (repo config, rawExpression) => same ResolvedTarget; never throws (unresolved is a value, not an error).

api.name: makeExternalEndpointId
api.signature: makeExternalEndpointId(repo: string, protocol: string, target: string, rawExpression?: string): string

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: In the id so endpoints dedup per-repo (ac2) and differ across repos.

parameters.name: target
parameters.purpose: The resolved identity, or '' when unresolved.

parameters.name: rawExpression
parameters.purpose: Used for the id when target==='' (unresolved), so an unresolved endpoint still has a stable id.

returns.meaning: sc1 (S001) — CONSUMED unchanged. The deterministic hex-32 per-repo endpoint id. N call-sites to one target+repo => one id => one node (ac2/k2).

preconditions: protocol/target derived from the ResolvedTarget returned by sc2.resolve.
postconditions: Stable across re-index; identical for every call-site reaching the same target in the same repo.

api.name: upsertEntities

parameters.name: entities
parameters.purpose: The externalEndpoint node(s) minted for resolved+unresolved targets.

returns.meaning: Existing API (src/db/entities.ts) — UNCHANGED. The post-parse pass upserts one externalEndpoint Entity per distinct id; keying by id gives dedup (ac2) for free.

postconditions: One node per distinct endpoint id exists after the pass.

errorCases.scenario: An HTTP call-site's URL argument cannot be extracted as an expression at all (e.g. the client call is spread/applied dynamically, or the URL arg is missing in a malformed AST).
errorCases.detection: The per-language recognizer matches the client shape but its URL-argument extractor returns no node / empty string for the argument position.
errorCases.response: Skip emitting a CALLS_HTTP relation for that call-site rather than emitting one with an empty `to` (an empty rawExpression would collide all such sites onto one meaningless node). The intra-code CALLS edge (if any) is still emitted normally.
errorCases.userImpact: That one dynamic call-site is not represented as an HTTP boundary (a recall gap), but no bogus/empty endpoint node is created; every extractable call-site is unaffected.

errorCases.scenario: The post-parse endpoint-resolution pass references a calling entity id (the CALLS_HTTP `from`) that no longer exists (the file was deleted/re-indexed between parse and the pass).
errorCases.detection: At edge-upsert time the pass looks up the `from` entity and finds no row (or the unresolved CALLS_HTTP relation has no live source entity).
errorCases.response: Skip that edge (upsert the endpoint node only if another live call-site references it; drop the dangling relation) rather than writing an edge from a non-existent entity. On the next re-index the relation is re-derived from the current source.
errorCases.userImpact: A transient mid-reindex race drops one edge; it reappears on the completed index. No crash, no dangling edge.

errorCases.scenario: The existing code-symbol resolver (Pass 2) picks up an unresolved CALLS_HTTP relation and tries to resolve its raw URL to a code entity.
errorCases.detection: A CALLS_HTTP relation appears in the code-symbol resolver's unresolved-relation walk (kind not excluded), and its `to` (a raw URL) matches no entity name.
errorCases.response: The code-symbol resolver EXCLUDES CALLS_HTTP (and the other boundary kinds) from its walk by design, so it never touches them; a regression is caught by a test asserting the resolver leaves CALLS_HTTP untouched for the S003 pass.
errorCases.userImpact: None when the exclusion holds; if it regressed, the endpoint edge would be mis-marked — which the exclusion test prevents at build time.

edgeCases.input: Several call-sites in one repo call the same resolved HTTP target (e.g. three `fetch(cfg.apiBase + '/x')` reaching api.example.com/x).
edgeCases.expected: One externalEndpoint node for that target (deduped by the deterministic per-repo id, ac2) with three separate CALLS_HTTP edges, one per calling entity.

edgeCases.input: Two different repos each call the same HTTP target (api.example.com).
edgeCases.expected: Two distinct externalEndpoint nodes — one per repo — because repo is part of the deterministic id; S003 never merges across repos (cross-repo linking is s8/s9).

edgeCases.input: An HTTP call whose URL cannot be pinned from any config source (resolved:false), e.g. `fetch(userInput)`.
edgeCases.expected: An unresolved externalEndpoint node (id derived from the rawExpression) carrying rawExpression, plus a CALLS_HTTP edge to it — never dropped (k5). A later config change can upgrade it on re-index.

edgeCases.input: A non-HTTP call that happens to share a name token with an HTTP client (e.g. a local function named `get` unrelated to axios).
edgeCases.expected: The recognizer keys on the client shape (receiver/import + call pattern), not the bare method name, so a local `get()` is NOT flagged as HTTP — it stays a plain CALLS edge (precision over false positives).

edgeCases.input: The same literal URL appears in two languages within one repo (a TS and a Python call to https://api.example.com/v1).
edgeCases.expected: One externalEndpoint node (the id is language-agnostic — repo+protocol+identity), with a CALLS_HTTP edge from each language's call-site; language does not fragment the endpoint.

edgeCases.input: An HTTP client call with an interpolated URL whose pieces all pin via sc2 (e.g. `${API_HOST}/users` with API_HOST in .env).
edgeCases.expected: resolved:true with the concrete identity as target; one node keyed on the resolved identity (so it dedups with a literal call to the same resolved host/path).

invariantsToPreserve.text: The existing code-symbol relation resolution (CALLS/INHERITS/IMPORTS -> entity ids) is unchanged: adding CALLS_HTTP emission + its dedicated pass must not alter how intra-code relations are detected or resolved; a repo with no HTTP calls produces a byte-identical graph to before.

Detection adds NO second parse pass — the HTTP recognizer runs inside the single existing tree-sitter call_expression walk; endpoint resolution is one bounded per-repo async pass, not a per-file or per-call-site rescan (performance NF).

Endpoint identity is the sc1 deterministic per-repo id (repo + 'externalEndpoint' + protocol + ':' + target||rawExpression); S003 mints ids only through makeExternalEndpointId so re-indexing is stable/idempotent and per-repo dedup holds (k2).

alternativesConsidered.name: Unresolved-CALLS_HTTP relation channel + a new async post-parse endpoint-resolution pass
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Per-language call_expression visitors push an UNRESOLVED CALLS_HTTP relation {from: callerId, to: rawUrlExpr, resolved:false} during the existing sync parse; a new async per-repo pass (after full parse) resolves each via sc2, mints the deduped externalEndpoint node, and upserts the resolved edge — reusing the existing unresolved-relation plumbing with ParseResult unchanged.
pros: Zero change to the ParseResult contract or the sync CodeParser signature — the detector is a thin plugin inside the existing parse (HLD 'thin plugins inside the existing tree-sitter parse'; performance NF: no second parse).
Reuses the established unresolved-relation channel + the existing 2-pass (parse then async per-repo resolver) shape, so endpoint resolution mirrors how code-symbol relations already resolve.
The async boundary is honored cleanly: sc2.resolve (async, per-repo, memoized) runs once per repo in the post-parse pass, not per-file, sharing one ConfigSourceMap build.
Deterministic dedup falls out of makeExternalEndpointId + upsertEntities keying by id (ac2), with repo in the id keeping cross-repo nodes distinct.
Idempotent re-index: same sources -> same relations -> same resolved ids/nodes (durability NF).
cons: CALLS_HTTP relations temporarily live 'unresolved' with a raw URL in `to` between parse and the post-parse pass — the resolver dispatch must route them to the S003 pass, an explicit exclusion the code must get right.

The endpoint node is minted in the post-parse pass, not at parse time, so a partial index (crash between parse and the pass) leaves unresolved CALLS_HTTP rows with no endpoint node until the pass re-runs (recoverable on re-index).

alternativesConsidered.name: Explicit httpCallSites[] intermediate on ParseResult + new async pass
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a typed `httpCallSites: HttpCallSite[]` field to ParseResult; parsers populate it during the walk; the same async post-parse pass consumes it to resolve + mint nodes/edges — an explicit intermediate rather than overloading the relation channel.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Functionally equivalent to a1 and slightly cleaner typing (no overloaded unresolved relation), but changes the ParseResult contract (a new field every parser + the indexer must thread) and introduces a second in-flight persistence shape for pending call-sites — a wider blast radius than a1 for no acceptance-criterion gain, and diverging from the codebase's existing emit-unresolved-then-resolve pattern. (s3: winnerRank 2.)

alternativesConsidered.name: Eager in-parse resolution (make the parse path async / add a sync resolver)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Resolve the URL and mint the endpoint node during the parse itself — either by making CodeParser.parse async so it can await sc2.resolve, or by exposing a synchronous resolver variant the parser can call inline.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Reaches the acceptance outcomes but only by either making all 5 parsers + the indexer async (a large surface change against the HLD 'thin plugin' boundary + performance NF) or coupling the pure per-file parse to a threaded ConfigSourceMap — partial on sc2, re-doing per-file what sc2 batches per-repo, for no benefit over a1's clean post-parse pass. (s3: violates/partial sc2.)
